# Forward guidance host acceptance

This candidate was authored by a fresh Luna host from the source AGENTS.md,
canonical CLI instructions and the existing synthetic ECON902 proposal, not
from a supplied answer. Inputs are created by
`scripts/create-guidance-host-acceptance.mjs`: invented syllabus/common guide,
two graded memo prompts and two selected current cached own-feedback values.
One superseded feedback value remains archived but is not selected.

Only the synthetic proposal UUID is replaced with `{{TASK_ID}}` here. Candidate
content is otherwise retained, not repaired to manufacture a passing replay.
The original host made seven CLI calls: four help commands, failed `task show`
(exit 1, proposal IDs were not supported), then two successful guidance saves.
It used directory inspection to recover the existing proposal; no replacement
was created. The retry created v2 and left v1 byte-identical. Thirteen original
vault files were independently hashed: only proposal.json changed (saved list).
The candidate preserves the existing prep sections, separates prompt-specific
graded memo headings, and incorporates assumptions/causal-limit lessons without
claiming feedback authorship, grading chronology or real-course permission.

That discovery failure prompted metadata-only guidance list/show commands.
Automated replay uses those commands with fresh CLI processes, checks context
selection/output versions and original bytes. Replay is regression coverage,
not another independent forward host, academic grading, native plugin injection
or an actual `/goal` interruption. Human review/redaction/activation remains
separate. The first host did not activate any guide.

A second fresh Luna host later used the added guidance list/show commands with
only config/course to recover the same ID and inspect both outputs/context.
Five discovery/help CLI calls succeeded. It wrote only a recovery report outside
the vault and did not re-save or activate anything. Its report correctly kept
activation/currentness/academic quality unverified. Parent reconstruction of the
initial record hash confirms that only saved-version metadata changed across
the first host's saves and the second host's read-only recovery.
